mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 0.25% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.25% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in UNRATE above 5% and a fall in PAYEMS below its 12-month moving average signals labor market imbalances, which increase cost pressures without corresponding employment growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in HOUST above its 6-month moving average for five consecutive months signals rising housing demand, which correlates with increased consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in CPIAUCSL below 1.5% over three months signals a restrictive monetary policy with subdued inflation, which increases discount rates but does not erode real earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL < 1.5% for three months
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy with low inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals rising household savings, which often precedes increased consumer spending and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered periods.
